title: The Social Construction of Reality
text:
This concept posits that human knowledge and understanding are not derived solely from objective external reality, but are instead shaped by collective agreement and social interaction. Meanings, norms, and categories—such as gender or currency value—exist because groups of people agree they exist within a given cultural context.

Sociological analysis emphasizes that perceived truths can be entirely contingent upon the dominant discursive framework of a community. Changes in social power dynamics often correspond with shifts in which 'realities' are deemed legitimate and worthy of belief.
